name: Schizoaffective disorder
summary: Psychotic illness meeting criteria for schizophrenia with concurrent major mood episodes, plus at least 2 weeks of psychosis without mood symptoms. Only oral paliperidone and monthly paliperidone palmitate (Invega Sustenna, Erzofri) carry a specific FDA indication; clozapine is labeled for reducing recurrent suicidal behavior in schizoaffective disorder.
plainSummary: Schizoaffective disorder combines symptoms of psychosis, like hearing voices or false beliefs, with mood episodes such as depression or mania. Only a few medicines are FDA-approved specifically for it, but others are often used.

approved.indication: Treatment of schizoaffective disorder as monotherapy and as an adjunct to mood stabilizers and/or antidepressants (efficacy established in two 6-week trials in adults).

population.ages: Adults (schizoaffective indication studied in adults only)

dosing.notes: Increase in 3 mg/day steps at intervals of more than 4 days. Renal impairment: CrCl 50 to <80 mL/min start 3 mg, max 6 mg/day; CrCl 10 to <50 mL/min start 1.5 mg, max 3 mg/day; not recommended if CrCl <10 mL/min. Swallow whole.

boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone, risperidone, or any excipient
approved.plainSummary: A once-daily pill that treats the psychosis and mood symptoms of schizoaffective disorder, alone or with a mood stabilizer or antidepressant.

approved.indication: Treatment of schizoaffective disorder in adults as monotherapy and as an adjunct to mood stabilizers or antidepressants.

dosing.start: 234 mg IM (deltoid) on day 1, then 156 mg IM (deltoid) on day 8
dosing.target: 78–234 mg IM monthly (deltoid or gluteal), starting 5 weeks after the first injection
dosing.notes: Establish tolerability with oral paliperidone or risperidone first. Mild renal impairment (CrCl 50 to <80 mL/min): 156 mg day 1, 117 mg day 8, then 78 mg monthly; not recommended if CrCl <50 mL/min. Missed-dose regimens in label.

formulations: Extended-release injectable suspension, prefilled syringe (39, 78, 117, 156, 234 mg)
boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone, risperidone, or any excipient
approved.plainSummary: A shot given once a month by a health professional that treats schizoaffective disorder without needing a daily pill.

verified.note: Generic paliperidone palmitate (e.g., Tolmar) has a DailyMed listing, but US market availability of generic 1-month injection was not independently confirmed.

approved.indication: Treatment of schizoaffective disorder in adults as monotherapy and as an adjunct to mood stabilizers or antidepressants.

dosing.start: 351 mg IM (deltoid) on day 1 (single initiation injection)
dosing.target: 78–234 mg IM monthly (deltoid or gluteal), starting 4 weeks after the first injection
dosing.notes: Establish tolerability with oral paliperidone or risperidone first. Unlike Invega Sustenna, no day-8 injection. Mild renal impairment uses a lower initiation (234 mg day 1) and maintenance dose per label; the 39 mg strength was not studied in the long-term schizoaffective trial.

formulations: Extended-release injectable suspension, prefilled syringe (39, 78, 117, 156, 234, 351 mg)
boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to paliperidone, risperidone, or any excipient
approved.plainSummary: A monthly paliperidone shot that starts with a single larger first dose instead of two starting shots.

approved.indication: Reducing the risk of recurrent suicidal behavior in patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder who are judged to be at chronic risk for re-experiencing suicidal behavior.

dosing.target: 300–450 mg/day in divided doses by the end of week 2 (increase by 25–50 mg/day)
dosing.notes: Baseline ANC required; do not start if ANC <1500/μL (<1000/μL with benign ethnic neutropenia); ANC monitoring per label schedule. Label suggests continuing at least 2 years for suicidal behavior. Re-titrate after ≥2 days missed. Reduce dose with strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. The Clozapine REMS was eliminated in 2025; ANC monitoring recommendations remain in labeling.

boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
contraindications: Known serious hypersensitivity to clozapine (e.g., photosensitivity, vasculitis, erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome) or any component
approved.plainSummary: Clozapine is the one medicine approved to lower the risk of repeated suicide attempts in schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder; it needs regular blood tests.

offLabel.agent: Other second-generation antipsychotics (e.g., risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole, ziprasidone) including their long-acting injectables
offLabel.use: Primary antipsychotic treatment of schizoaffective disorder (labeled for schizophrenia and/or bipolar disorder but not specifically for schizoaffective disorder)
offLabel.notes: Trials of these agents often enrolled mixed schizophrenia/schizoaffective samples; treatment is commonly extrapolated from schizophrenia and bipolar data. In a Finnish/Swedish nationwide cohort, LAIs and clozapine were associated with the lowest psychosis rehospitalization risk, while quetiapine was not associated with reduced risk. Usual antipsychotic metabolic, movement, and prolactin monitoring applies.

details.labeledFor: Risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole, and ziprasidone are FDA-approved for schizophrenia and/or bipolar I disorder; only paliperidone carries a schizoaffective indication.

dosing.start: Risperidone 1–2 mg, olanzapine 5–10 mg, aripiprazole 10–15 mg, or ziprasidone 40 mg twice daily
dosing.target: Usual schizophrenia ranges (risperidone 4–8 mg, olanzapine 10–20 mg, aripiprazole 15–30 mg, ziprasidone 80–160 mg/day)
dosing.max: Labeled maximums (risperidone 16, olanzapine 20, aripiprazole 30, ziprasidone 160 mg/day)
dosing.notes: Long-acting injectables of these drugs are used to protect against relapse.

formulations: Risperidone, olanzapine, aripiprazole oral and long-acting injectables
boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in young people (aripiprazole)
contraindications: Ziprasidone: QT prolongation, recent MI, uncompensated heart failure, or QT-prolonging drugs
warnings: Ziprasidone: QT prolongation; take with food
details.plainSummary: Doctors commonly use the same antipsychotics as for schizophrenia in schizoaffective disorder, even though only one oral and one injection are labeled for it.

references.label: Lintunen J et al. Long-term real-world effectiveness of pharmacotherapies for schizoaffective disorder. Schizophr Bull 2021

offLabel.agent: Mood stabilizers (lithium, valproate/divalproex, lamotrigine) added to an antipsychotic
offLabel.use: Adjunct for mood symptoms, especially bipolar-type schizoaffective disorder
offLabel.notes: Evidence is mainly observational and extrapolated from bipolar disorder; combination with antipsychotics was associated with reduced psychosis rehospitalization in a nationwide cohort. Lithium requires serum level, renal, and thyroid monitoring; valproate carries hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, and teratogenicity warnings (avoid in people who may become pregnant when alternatives exist).

details.labeledFor: Lithium and valproate are FDA-approved for bipolar disorder (and valproate for epilepsy); lamotrigine for epilepsy and bipolar I maintenance; none is labeled for schizoaffective disorder.

dosing.start: Lithium 300 mg twice daily; divalproex 250–500 mg twice daily; lamotrigine 25 mg/day with slow titration
dosing.target: Lithium level 0.6–1.0 mEq/L; valproate trough 50–100 mcg/mL; lamotrigine 100–200 mg/day
dosing.max: Labeled limits apply (lamotrigine 200 mg/day for bipolar)
dosing.notes: Add to an antipsychotic for mood symptoms.

formulations: Lithium capsules, tablets, ER tablets, solution
contraindications: Valproate: hepatic disease, urea cycle disorders, mitochondrial disease
warnings: Lithium: serum level, renal, and thyroid monitoring
Lamotrigine: slow titration to limit rash
details.plainSummary: Mood stabilizers are added to an antipsychotic for the mood swings in schizoaffective disorder. Each needs its own safety monitoring.

references.label: Lintunen J et al. Schizophr Bull 2021 (nationwide cohorts)
APA Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia, 3rd ed. Am J Psychiatry 2020

offLabel.agent: Antidepressants (e.g., SSRIs) added to an antipsychotic
offLabel.use: Adjunct for depressive episodes in depressive-type schizoaffective disorder
offLabel.notes: Data are largely extrapolated from schizophrenia trials (small benefit for depressive and negative symptoms) and observational cohorts with inconsistent results. Monitor for activation, mania/switching in bipolar-type illness, QT prolongation with some combinations, and CYP2D6 interactions with antipsychotics.

details.labeledFor: SSRIs are FDA-approved for depression and anxiety disorders; none is labeled for schizoaffective disorder.

dosing.start: Sertraline 25–50 mg or escitalopram 5–10 mg daily
dosing.target: Usual antidepressant ranges (sertraline 50–200 mg, escitalopram 10–20 mg)

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOI use within 14 days (or linezolid / IV methylene blue)
warnings: Early activation or anxiety, GI upset, sexual dysfunction
Hyponatremia and bleeding risk (higher with NSAIDs/anticoagulants)
Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
Switch to mania in bipolar-type illness
QT prolongation with some antipsychotic combinations
details.plainSummary: Antidepressants may be added for depressive episodes in schizoaffective disorder, usually alongside an antipsychotic.

references.label: Helfer B et al. Antidepressants added to antipsychotics for schizophrenia: meta-analysis. Am J Psychiatry 2016
Lintunen J et al. Schizophr Bull 2021

offLabel.use: Treatment-resistant schizoaffective disorder (clozapine is labeled only for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and for suicidal behavior in schizoaffective disorder)
offLabel.notes: Observational nationwide data associate clozapine with the lowest risk of psychosis rehospitalization in schizoaffective disorder. Requires ANC monitoring and attention to myocarditis, seizures, orthostasis, constipation/ileus, and metabolic effects.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and reducing suicidal behavior in schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder; not for treatment-resistant schizoaffective disorder as such.

dosing.target: Increase by 25–50 mg/day toward 300–450 mg/day; use levels to guide
dosing.notes: Follow the clozapine ANC monitoring schedule on the current label.

boxedWarnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis
warnings: Myocarditis, especially in the first month
details.plainSummary: Clozapine is the strongest antipsychotic and is used when schizoaffective disorder has not responded to other medicines. It needs regular blood tests.

references.label: Lintunen J et al. Schizophr Bull 2021
